senses.gloss:
पल

PALA . A measure of ancient times. (See under trasareṇu).

पाल

PĀLA . A serpent born of the race of vāsuki. This serpent committed suicide at the sarpasatra of janamejaya. (Śloka 51, Chapter 57, Ādi Parva).

पालक

PĀLAKA . A son born to the King caṇḍamahāsena of his wife aṅgāravatī. aṅgāravatī got two sons. The other son was named gopālaka. (Kathāmukhalambaka, kathāsaritsāgara).

पालकाव्य

PĀLAKĀVYA . The author of the famous book ‘Hastyāyurvedasaṁhitā’. This book contains 160 chapters dealing with Mahārogasthāna (great diseases), Kṣudrarogasthāna (minor diseases), Śalyasthāna (extraction of extraneous matter from the body) and Uttarasthāna (diseases of the head). pālakāvya taught this Āyurvedasaṁhitā to Rāmapāda, King of Aṅgadeśa. (agni purāṇa).

पलाला

PALĀLĀ . One of the seven mothers of subrahmaṇya. The other six are: kākī, halimā, Brahmikā, mālinī, āryā and mitrā. (Śloka 10, Chapter 228, Vana Parva).

पलाशवन

PALĀŚAVANA . A sacred forest. Once the sage jamadagni performed a sacrifice in this forest. On that occasion all the rivers in the world were present there carrying their water. The sage at this Yāga gave wine to all the other sages to their heart's content. (Śloka 16, Chapter 94, Vana Parva).

पाली

PĀLĪ . A corrupt form of Sanskrit.

पलित

PALITA . A rat, a character in ‘Biḍālopākhyāna’. This rat held a conversation with lomaśa, a cat. (See under biḍālopākhyāna).

पालिता

PĀLITĀ . A female follower of subrahmaṇya. (Śloka 3, Chapter 46, śalya Parva).

पल्लाण्टु

PALLĀṆṬU . The name of the devotional songs sung by the Tamil devotional poet, Visṇucittar.
